First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{sin}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3 & =0 \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =3 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(1)=\frac{\pi }{2}
$$

Since $\frac{\pi }{2}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ 

As this is a quadrantal angle, to find the remaining solutions, we use our knowledge of the sine function. We know that the sine function has its maximum values at:

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi 
$$

Since the domain $-\pi <x\le \pi $ is one period, and we have already found one maximum value in this period, we conclude that $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ is the only solution.
